messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: distributions refactor
parts:
I just took a long pass through the prob/distributions
and boy are my fingers tired. There are over 25
distribution functions, each in its own file with its
own tests (which I think makes more sense than the way
I originally had it in one big file).

1. There are still some errors in values for unit
tests. But the build's not failing.

Daniel -- could you (a) fix the code (or tests) so
the tests pass, and (b) fix the makefile so that
failing tests cause failure?

2. I changed all "" includes to <> just for
consistency. We need to figure out the right way
to do this globally.

3. I moved files like prob/distributions_foo.hpp
to either prob/distributions/foo.hpp
or just to prob/foo.hpp.

There's no need to mock up a directory structure in a
file name. There's still some vestiges of my
earlier flatter structure around we should get rid of
in test names.

4. We need more includes on a per-file basis.
Specifically, if we have an independent file
for include, it should include everything it needs.
We have massive problems as I indicated in the previous
mail with things just getting brought in at a very
high-level scope when it should be lower.

It'd be really great if Daniel, Matt and I could sit
down and work out how we want this to work. I may
have the wrong end of things here.

One issue is the namespace for agrad operations. I'd
originally put these in their own namespace, which
means you can't write:

z = stan::maths::log_sum_exp(y)

because the agrad version is in its own name space

z = stan::agrad::log_sum_exp(y).

Maybe the agrad versions should match the namespaces of the
original functions? Otherwise, we'll need:

using stan::maths::log_sum_exp;
using stan::agrad::log_sum_exp;

z = log_sum_exp(y);

There's really no way to get around functions like

boost::math::lgamma()

unless we want a shadow lgamma() in stan::maths, which
might make sense.

5. As to style, I have a few requests:

a. Try to keep lines 80 characters or under if
possible -- it's hard to scan through them otherwise.

b. if (cond) ... OVER if(cond) ...

c. foo(x) OVER foo (x)

d. no tabs. I realize I haven't configured emacs to
do this for cpp for me automatically. We can script
replacements perhaps and I'll change my emacses. Here's
the magic juju:

http://lingpipe-blog.com/2006/07/28/spring-cleaning-lingpipe-with-pmd-and-fixcrlf-and-emacs/

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] distributions refactor
parts:
Happy New Year!

Regarding 1: yeah, I was working through fixing the changes made, but
if you've already got that done, I'll go on and fix the unit tests.
I've been working on them one at a time getting the include_summand's
in there and moving them over. For the makefile, do you want the build
to fail on unit test failures? That is, once a test fails, the build
stops?

Let's walk through this stuff in person this week. Tuesday? Wednesday
after the meeting?


Daniel
